content.thinking:
I'm planning a frost axe design that stands upright on a small ice plinth with the haft socketed into it, sized to real battle-axe proportions around 1.3 meters tall overall so it touches the floor as required.

I'll include a single root joint since objects likely still need one even without moving parts, and keep part construction limited to the core primitives like part, extrude, lathe, sweep, rod, spike, glow, and paint.

For the asymmetric look, I'm orienting the blade to extend sideways in the viewing plane with a large crescent edge on one side and a smaller spiked ice-crystal fluke on the back, then working out exact y-coordinates for the plinth, haft, and head placement.

Now I'm plotting the crescent blade outline point by point, shaping a bearded axe profile with upper and lower horn tips, a convex cutting edge bulging outward, and a concave inner notch curving back toward the eye socket.

I'm planning a thickness taper of 0.035 with a 0.01 bevel for sharpness, and using a custom paint function to brighten the blade near the cutting edge based on position, fading from dark steel-blue at the socket to white at the tip for a frosty effect.

For style, I'll go with a hand-painted, stylized glow using color mixing for the paint. The blade sits on the +X side, extruded from the haft origin with the outline overlapping the socket collar, while the back gets a smaller mirrored spike or fluke on the -X side.

I'm shaping the back fluke as fanning ice crystal shards using cone geometry, plus a tall crystalline spear tip rising above the haft. For the haft itself, I'm keeping it a straight rod with wrapped bands, painted in a dark frosted navy-blue wood grain.

For the grip, I'm adding alternating leather torus wraps oriented horizontally along the haft, with a hexagonal stone plinth at the base topped with icicles and frost crystals. At the head, I'm lathing an ornate socket collar around the haft to anchor everything together.

Now I'm defining the color palette—gold trim, dark steel, icy blues and whites—and placing gold torus rings at both ends, plus planning a rune decal texture on the blade face near the bevel edge.

Writing SVG decal code...

Working out the inset edge coordinates for the curved path...

I'm now planning a decorative snowflake motif with six arms placed at (28,40), sized so it sits inside the blade's notch without crossing edges, plus a small crescent accent nearby.

For the icy texture itself, I'm figuring out how to add an edge-lit highlight: approximating the blade's outline as an ellipse-like shape and computing a radial distance measure so I can apply a smoothstep gradient that brightens to white near the cutting edge.

Darkening the steel blue in the interior, adding cell-noise cracks as thin lighter lines, and painting pale near-white tones along horizontal walls for that icy highlight. I'm also weighing whether to apply a cel-shading toon effect specifically on the blade for a painted, LoL-style look, deciding to try it carefully since the signature should accept a plain color input.

Now I'm sketching the back fluke shape as an extruded spike profile, testing a few coordinate sequences to get a forward-curving, sharp-tipped point while making sure the resulting outline stays a simple, non-self-intersecting polygon.

Then I'm moving on to the ice crystal cluster sitting atop the fluke — thinking of using faceted cone and hexagonal cylinder shapes with flat shading for a crystalline look, in icy blue tones, plus a tall central spike built from a base point, direction, length, and radius.

I'm also planning an ornamental gold cup beneath the spike and a hanging ice-blue ribbon of cloth draped from the collar area, tapered with a swallow-tail end, positioned slightly in front of the haft.

Shaping the swallowtail outline...

I'm lathing a hexagonal plinth base with a snowy stone surface, painting it gray-blue with mottled patches and white snow where the surface normal points upward, plus squashed sphere snow mounds on top.

Now I'm scattering icicle shards around the plinth edge as tilted cones in icy color, then shaping a wider second plinth tier with a stepped lathe profile.

Checking overall proportions next: haft rod running from 0.1 to 1.3, head centered at 1.0 with blade extending 0.67 forward and fluke 0.58 back, spike tip reaching 1.6 total—all comfortably within the target height and stable on the 0.42-radius plinth. For the grip, I'm planning alternating torus rings along the haft merged into a single geometry using BufferGeometryUtils.

Simplifying the grip to a painted rod with dark/light leather stripes and a wobble effect, plus gold torus rings capping each end, with a diagonal spiral wrap achieved through stripe painting along the surface parameter. I also want frosted grain detailing near the top of the haft, blending wood tones into a pale hoarfrost gradient.

I'll skip card details and instead scatter small frost crystal cones at random heights along the shaft. For the core gem, I'm placing a small glowing cyan sphere in a gold torus setting on the collar's front face, with a matching gem on the back, sized to overlap the collar slightly for a seated look. For the gold filigree, I'm sketching an outline plate bracket sandwiching the blade root, slightly wider than the blade itself to frame it.

Adjusting plate outline coordinates...

I'll skip blade serrations but add a handful of ice shards jutting out near the blade's spine for texture, then mirror the rune plane on the opposite face for symmetry.

Now I'm setting up the glow effect, export metadata, and the root joint, keeping imports limited to only what's actually used to satisfy TypeScript's strictness.

Writing blade paint function...

Checking the lighting threshold against face normals for the cel shading effect, then defining the plinth paint logic with a snow cap and stone texture beneath.

For the haft, I'm layering a wood grain texture with a frost gradient that creeps upward from the base and separately at the top where it meets the head.

Now I'm writing a shard helper that positions a cone at a given point with its base anchored along a direction vector, then using it to scatter ice shards across the blade faces near the root.

I'm placing icicle shards along the lower edge interpolating between key points, then adding upward-growing crystals on the top inner edge and a small ice cluster crown near the fluke tip, before moving on to collar details like gold rings.

Now I'm sketching helper functions for torus rings and ribbon cloth geometry at the front and back, with painting logic to give the fabric a cel-shaded blue with a gold hem trim along the edges.

I'm adding small gold tassel bead spheres at the ribbon ends, plus gold rings on the haft below the grip for decoration. Then I'm planning placement of icicle spikes around the plinth base using a seeded random for angle jitter, working out their radii and heights across the stepped tiers before writing out all the final coordinates.

I'm placing flattened sphere shapes as snow mounds on top of the plinth, scaling them thin and wide to look like accumulated snow, with five mounds scattered around. Then I need to make sure the outline point arrays are properly typed with the "sharp" literal, importing the OutlinePoint type and annotating variables so TypeScript doesn't complain.
